chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Arafat, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) who said:

The one who is not content with sustenance except in abundance, will not be satisfied with deeds except in abundance; and the one who is content with little sustenance, indeed he will be satisfied with little deeds.
ai.seo_question: How does contentment with wealth affect one's performance in religious duties?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) to illustrate the spiritual principle that inner satisfaction with worldly provision (rizq) directly influences one's capacity for consistent religious observance (amal). This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that greed creates a distraction of the heart, leading to negligence in worship, while contentment fosters the spiritual focus necessary for diligence, even in small deeds.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Arafat, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who is not content from the sustenance except with a lot, would not be sufficed with from the deeds except a lot; and the one who suffices from the little sustenance, so he would be sufficed from the little deeds’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn ‘Arafah from abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Whoever is not satisfied with anything but a large quantity of sustenance, his deeds will not be enough unless they are a great deal. Whoever is comfortable with little amount of sustenance, even little good deeds will be sufficient for him.”
